method: Loose-tube fiber cables name both buffer tubes and the fibers inside them with a repeating 12-color sequence: 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 green, 4 brown, 5 slate, 6 white, 7 red, 8 black, 9 yellow, 10 violet, 11 rose and 12 aqua. Tubes are counted from the start of the cable, so the tube is ceil(fiber / fibersPerTube) and the fiber's position in that tube is ((fiber - 1) mod fibersPerTube) + 1. The tube color is color number ((tube - 1) mod 12) + 1 and the fiber color is color number ((position - 1) mod 12) + 1. A 6-fiber tube uses only the first six colors; a 24-fiber tube repeats the 12 colors in a second pass at positions 13 to 24; tube colors repeat after tube 12. Each repeat group is marked by a tracer, stripe or binder, the exact marking varies by manufacturer, and the tool therefore reports the repeat group without naming the physical marker. Fiber numbers are whole numbers from 1 to 288, fibers per tube is 6, 12 or 24, and blank, fractional, negative and out-of-range values are refused with the failing field named rather than defaulted.

sources.title: TIA-598-D, Optical Fiber Cable Color Coding: the twelve-color sequence blue, orange, green, brown, slate, white, red, black, yellow, violet, rose, aqua is applied to both fibers and buffer tubes.

Loose-tube cable construction: fibers are grouped in color-coded buffer tubes, tubes are numbered from the start of the cable, and later groups repeat the colors with a manufacturer-specific tracer or binder.
